title: PromQL Fundamentals
intro: PromQL is how you ask Prometheus questions. A handful of patterns — rate, sum by, ratios, and time windows — answer the vast majority of real questions.

steps.prompt: Show every scrape target and whether its last scrape succeeded.
steps.fake_output:
up{instance="web01:9100", job="node"}        1
up{instance="web02:9100", job="node"}        0
up{instance="api:8080", job="checkout-service"} 1
steps.explanation: 1 = scraped OK, 0 = scrape failed. web02's exporter is unreachable.
steps.why: 'up' is Prometheus's own synthetic metric for every target. It's the first thing to check when a dashboard shows 'No data' — it tells you whether Prometheus even has the data.

steps.prompt: Show total requests per second, summed per service instead of per individual pod.
steps.explanation: rate() first computes per-series per-second rates; sum by (service) then aggregates across pods.
steps.why: Always rate() BEFORE sum(). Summing raw counters first and then taking the rate breaks whenever any single pod restarts and its counter resets to zero.

steps.prompt: How many 500 errors happened in the last hour, as a total count?
steps.explanation: increase() gives the total growth over the window instead of a per-second rate.
steps.why: rate() suits graphs and alerts; increase() suits human-readable totals ('412 errors in the last hour'). Mathematically, increase is just rate × window length.

steps.prompt: What fraction of memory is still available on each node?
steps.explanation: Division between series with matching labels. db01 has only 4% of memory available.
steps.why: Ratios are more useful than raw bytes for alerting — 'below 10% available' works for every node size, while a raw-bytes threshold needs a different number per machine.

steps.prompt: Smooth out a spiky CPU metric by averaging it over the last 10 minutes.
steps.explanation: Averages each series' raw samples across the window.
steps.why: *_over_time functions (avg, max, min) work on gauges like CPU or queue depth. Don't use them on counters — use rate() there. Mixing up gauges and counters is the most common PromQL mistake.
